name: Orson Pratt
role: Missionary and member of the Quorum of the Twelve
dateNote: Section 34 came on 4 November 1830, weeks after his baptism on his nineteenth birthday.
importance: Section 34 calls the young convert Orson Pratt to preach and prophesy. Later revelations send him to Missouri in 1831, to the eastern states in 1832, and out to recruit for Zion in 1834. He became one of the first Twelve Apostles in 1835, was excommunicated in 1842, and was restored in 1843. Section 136 assigns him to organize a company for the trek west in 1847.
connections: He was baptized by his older brother Parley P. Pratt, and section 52 sends the brothers together. Other companions named with him include Lyman Johnson, Orson Hyde, and Wilford Woodruff.

sources.title: Orson Pratt, Joseph Smith Papers biography

reviewNote: Dates, ordinations, excommunication (20 Aug. 1842) and rebaptism (20 Jan. 1843) checked on JSP; death 3 Oct. 1881 read from a partly cut fragment. Bare “Orson” occurs only at 34:1 for him, but “Orson Hyde” appears elsewhere, so the linker must prefer the longer name. The note that he adapted section 129 for the 1876 edition comes from the 129 study file.
